title: Time Complexity of QuickSort #1
statement: What is the worst-case time complexity of standard QuickSort and when does it occur?

options.text: O(N log N), in all cases
O(N), when elements are reverse sorted
O(N^2), when the pivot is always the smallest or largest element in an already sorted array

explanation: When pivot partitioning is highly unbalanced (1 and N-1 elements), recursion depth is N leading to O(N^2).

title: Balanced BST Height Property #2
statement: What is the maximum height of an AVL Tree containing N nodes?
explanation: AVL trees strictly enforce a balance factor of {-1, 0, +1}, ensuring height is strictly bounded by ~1.44 log2(N).

title: Topological Sort Applicability #3
statement: Topological sorting is uniquely defined for which class of graphs?
explanation: Topological sort requires a directed graph without any cycles (DAG) to ensure linear vertex dependency ordering.

title: Floyd Warshall Dynamic Programming #4
statement: What is the time complexity of the Floyd-Warshall algorithm for All-Pairs Shortest Paths?
explanation: Floyd-Warshall uses three nested loops over all vertices V, resulting in O(V^3) time complexity.

title: Monotonic Stack Applications #5
statement: Which data structure is optimal for finding the "Next Greater Element" for every element in an array in O(N) total time?
explanation: A monotonic decreasing stack processes each element at most twice (one push, one pop), achieving O(N) overall time.

explanation: A monotonic decreasing stack processes each element at most twice (one push, one pop), achieving O(N) overall time.

title: Time Complexity of QuickSort #111
statement: What is the worst-case time complexity of standard QuickSort and when does it occur?

options.text: O(N log N), in all cases
O(N), when elements are reverse sorted
O(N^2), when the pivot is always the smallest or largest element in an already sorted array

explanation: When pivot partitioning is highly unbalanced (1 and N-1 elements), recursion depth is N leading to O(N^2).

title: Balanced BST Height Property #112
statement: What is the maximum height of an AVL Tree containing N nodes?
explanation: AVL trees strictly enforce a balance factor of {-1, 0, +1}, ensuring height is strictly bounded by ~1.44 log2(N).

title: Topological Sort Applicability #113
statement: Topological sorting is uniquely defined for which class of graphs?
explanation: Topological sort requires a directed graph without any cycles (DAG) to ensure linear vertex dependency ordering.

title: Floyd Warshall Dynamic Programming #114
statement: What is the time complexity of the Floyd-Warshall algorithm for All-Pairs Shortest Paths?
explanation: Floyd-Warshall uses three nested loops over all vertices V, resulting in O(V^3) time complexity.
